# paydecode

> paydecode is "jwt.io for agent payments": a browser tool that decodes agent-payment artifacts into plain English with risk flags. All decoding happens client-side; pasted input is never uploaded. Built by Agnij Dutta (@0xholmesdev).

Use it to inspect what an AI agent's payment authorization actually allows before it is sent or settled.

## What it decodes

- x402 v1 and v2 HTTP headers: `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` (402 challenge), `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` / `X-PAYMENT` (signed payment), `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` / `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (settlement receipt). Base64 JSON, header lines accepted.
- EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization` and Permit2 witness transfers, including EIP-712 domain checks against known USDC deployments (name, version, chain id, contract).
- AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) mandates: v0.2 SD-JWT mandates and `~~`-joined delegation chains (open and closed checkout/payment mandates), plus v0.1 Intent/Cart/Payment mandate JSON.
- Solana x402 payment transactions (partially signed versioned transactions with SPL TransferChecked).

## Risk flags it raises (examples)

- Authorization expired or not yet valid
- EIP-712 domain name mismatch (for example "USD Coin" vs "USDC" on Base Sepolia), which makes the signature recover to the wrong address
- Payment amount above the mandate cap, payee outside the allowed list
- Settlement failures and their error reasons

## Links

- App: https://paydecode.vercel.app/
- Source and npm library: https://github.com/agnij-dutta/paydecode
- Enforcement (on-chain spend caps for agents): https://capline-protocol.vercel.app
